story.title: From Dakar's Olympic Pool to Bahrain: Swimmer Hamed Al-Husaini Targets the Arab Championships
story.seo_title: Omani Swimmer Hamed Al-Husaini Eyes Arab Championships
story.meta_description: After competing at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, Omani swimmer Hamed Al-Husaini prepares for the 400m and 800m freestyle at the Arab Championships.

detail.extracted_title: From Dakar's Olympic Pool to Bahrain: Swimmer Hamed Al-Husaini Targets the Arab Championships
detail.excerpt: Fresh from his debut at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Senegal, young Omani distance swimmer Hamed Al-Husaini is applying his international racing lessons to the 400-meter and 800-meter freestyle at the upcoming Arab Swimming Championships in Bahrain.
detail.article_html:
For a young distance swimmer, the first appearance on an Olympic starting block is an education that no domestic training camp can replicate. At the Tour de l'Oeuf aquatic complex in Dakar, Senegal, Omani national team swimmer Hamed Al-Husaini recently completed his debut at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games—an experience he is now channeling directly into preparations for the Arab Swimming Championships in the Kingdom of Bahrain in mid-November.

Competing in the preliminary heats of the men's 400-meter freestyle in Dakar, Al-Husaini clocked a time of 4 minutes and 29.8 seconds, finishing second in his heat and 31st overall in a field of 33 international swimmers. While the result fell short of advancing to the final—where Saudi swimmer Rami Bilal Al-Rahmouni captured gold in 3:57.6, followed by Russia's Bogdan Torikhin (3:58.5) and Mexico's Daniel Grillo (4:02.6)—both Al-Husaini and his coaching staff view the Dakar campaign as a vital technical benchmark for his upcoming regional races.

Navigating Heat, Crowded Warm-Up Lanes, and Olympic Pressure

Reflecting on his Youth Olympic debut, Al-Husaini noted that racing alongside elite junior swimmers from across the world revealed the exact physical, pacing, and tactical margins required at the international level. Beyond the race itself, living inside the Youth Olympic Village exposed the Omani teenager to how top-ranked federations structure their pre-race recovery, nutrition, and mental preparation.

National aquatic team coach Mohammed Bouguerra, an Algerian specialist leading Al-Husaini's preparation, pointed out that the conditions in Dakar tested the swimmer's adaptability under pressure. High ambient temperatures at the Tour de l'Oeuf pool and crowded warm-up facilities caused by the large number of competing delegations limited pre-race water time. In fact, rising water temperatures at the venue prompted the organizing committee to cancel the men's 800-meter freestyle altogether—an event in which Al-Husaini had also been scheduled to compete.

Turning Olympic Lessons into Podium Contention in Bahrain

Rather than dwelling on the canceled 800-meter race, Bouguerra and the technical staff have immediately integrated the lessons from Dakar into Al-Husaini's training block for the Arab Swimming Championships in Bahrain. In mid-November, Al-Husaini will contest both his signature distance events: the 400-meter and 800-meter freestyle.

According to Bouguerra, observing Al-Husaini's stroke mechanics and split pacing against Olympic-caliber peers allowed the coaching team to pinpoint specific adjustments in turn efficiency, nutritional timing, and mid-race endurance. Meanwhile, Oman's broader campaign at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games continues on Sunday, November 8, at the Dakar Expo Center in Diamniadio, where Ziyad bin Ali Al-Balushi will compete in the men's under-48 kg taekwondo division on Sunday, followed on Tuesday, November 10, by fencer Jana Al-Sharji in the women's individual épée. For Hamed Al-Husaini, the road from Dakar's Olympic lanes leads straight to the starting blocks in Bahrain, armed with the composure of an athlete who has already tested himself on the world stage.

Sources

  • Oman Daily
detail.instagram_caption:
After completing his debut at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Senegal, young Omani national team swimmer Hamed Al-Husaini is turning his international racing experience toward the upcoming Arab Swimming Championships in the Kingdom of Bahrain in mid-November.

Competing in the 400-meter freestyle preliminaries at the Tour de l'Oeuf complex in Dakar, Al-Husaini clocked 4:29.8 to finish second in his heat against a 33-swimmer global field. Working alongside national coach Mohammed Bouguerra, Al-Husaini used the Olympic campaign to refine his race pacing, nutrition, and tactical preparation ahead of contesting both the 400-meter and 800-meter freestyle in Bahrain, while Omani teammates Ziyad Al-Balushi (taekwondo) and Jana Al-Sharji (fencing) prepare to enter Youth Olympic action in Dakar next week.

How important is early Youth Olympic exposure in building the next generation of Omani athletes?

Read the full analysis at omanspire.om (link in bio).
